⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6’s story is built around the relationship between Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and there is plenty in the game that showcases how in love they are.
  • According to recent reports, is that really for the best though?
  • She tells him that he needs to do better and envies those who have more than her.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6’s story is built around the relationship between Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, and there is plenty in the game that showcases how in love they are. Both of them go out of their way for each other, and stick together through thick and thin.

According to recent reports, is that really for the best though? Let’s be honest, Jason is a stud. He spends the beginning of the game putting in serious work to provide for his girl, and he even fixes up the house to make it a truly livable space.

What does Lucia do in return? She tells him that he needs to do better and envies those who have more than her. Let’s face it, she is a walking red flag.

Sources indicate that it is crucial to stay grounded and to make sure that you don’t want too much at times, and that is something that Lucia just can’t do. She is willing to do anything to make it big. Her immediate thought after getting out of prison is that she wants to someday be on a yacht.

That is not inherently a bad dream, but the willingness to go above and beyond by breaking the law on multiple accounts and accepting sketchy deals make it a red flag.

She can work hard, get back on her feet, and provide for her son. She doesn’t need to risk it all to get a lavish lifestyle that may ultimately end up with her back in prison.

According to recent reports, lucia spent time in prison, and she gets out shortly after the start of the game. You would think that Lucia would have learned to avoid crime after spending time in prison. Instead, it is the exact opposite.

She gets out of prison, and her first thought is to commit crimes in order to get money. She could let Jason keep doing his thing, but instead she calls up her friend and makes Jason ask about a job with them so that they can get more money.

She doesn’t care about staying out of trouble. Instead, she jumps straight back into it. It’s almost like she wants to get caught.

Sources indicate that there are a few rules that Lucia must abide by when she gets out of prison, with the most notable of them being that she is under house arrest. This requires her to wear an ankle monitor, and she is only allowed to stray about a half mile away from Jason’s home unless she is working.

In a recent development, while she pays attention to this rule at first, she ignores it the first chance she gets. While her ankle monitor is still on, she goes for a flight with Jason despite him advising her not to.

On top of this, when they have a chance to spend time with Kat and Mattia, she takes the opportunity to have her ankle monitor removed and goes for a night on the town.

It has been revealed that there is something to be said about someone who is willing to fight for what they believe in or rush to the defense of others. However, sometimes this can be a detriment and can hurt a relationship.

Recent findings suggest that lucia tends to have a very hot-blooded attitude. Meaning, she likes to pick fights when others are in the wrong, and she will defend her opinion until she dies.

If someone says something salty, Lucia is the first to snap back at them, and while it isn’t always good to stay quiet in every situation, there are times where she needs to learn to breathe, let it out, and move on instead of wanting to fight.

According to recent reports, lucia and Jason are like two sides of the same coin, but one side is focused on control while the other side is focused on chaos, and Lucia is the chaotic side. It is a fun dichotomy in the game, but in a relationship, this chaotic nature can get you killed.

Lucia likes to take the route of violence in most situations. She doesn’t stick to a blueprint, deciding instead to throw it out and improvise.

It is this impulsive nature that landed her in jail in the first place while she was separated from Jason, and it is the same chaotic nature that could possibly land both of them in jail if Jason wasn’t around to be a bit more logical. While Lucia gets things done, that type of chaos isn’t always healthy.

It has been revealed that throughout GTA 6, you are wanted, and it is sometimes difficult to get by, but Lucia has the attitude of never giving up, which means that she is willing to fight until she draws her last breath. While this can be good in some circumstances, when you are wanted by the cops, it can be a major downfall.

If this wasn’t a GTA game and someone had that attitude, they would be in a world of hurt when the cops came rolling in. Even when Jason was to the point of wanting to call it in, she refused, and she dictated that they never give up.

Eventually, this is bound to land her in even more hot water than she is already in, and she will only have herself to blame.

Lying is sometimes okay, but only when it is because you are trying to hide a gift for someone or maybe you tell a little white lie to your child. It isn’t okay to lie to your partner or the police, both of which Lucia does.

As soon as she gets caught doing something she wasn’t supposed to, which she caused because she refused to listen to Jason, she lied to her parole officer.

In her defense, the parole officer is a jerk and comes off as creepy, but that is still no reason to lie, and to force your partner to lie on your behalf is also wrong, yet for Lucia, this stuff comes naturally.

It has been revealed that there are a lot of people out there who like to party, and that is perfectly fine. They like to have a few drinks, kick back with their friends, and have a good time. Meanwhile, you have the few who are extreme party animals.

Sources indicate that they do drugs, hit the liquor hard, and party all night long. That is the type of girl Lucia can be, and that is a massive red flag for a lot of people.

Industry observers note that there are some online who have remarked that she is “for the streets” because of her willingness to let it all out and party all night long. As soon as she sees people wasting money on breaking champagne bottles and speeding through Vice City in nice cars, she immediately lets her party animal out of its cage and follows exactly what they do.

We are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a fresh video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - revealed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

Thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:.

You can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

Sources indicate that amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It seems like we’re getting one of these every few months, but the world of mobile action RPGs that look like the games that, just a few years back, were only possible on consoles is expanding with another new entry.

Netmarble, a studio and publisher known for its free-to-play games on mobile and PC, recently unveiled the launch date for The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin, its next major release that’s very much coming for the Genshin Impact crowd.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin is an open-world action RPG based on the world of The Seven Deadly Sins anime and manga. The game takes place in the world of Britannia, which looks similar to the way it does in the anime.

That stated, the story of the game is not based on the anime or manga, Instead, it’s an original story set in the universe of the show. You play as Prince Tristan of the Kingdom of Liones who must find a way to bring order back to Britannia.

The gameplay should be familiar to anyone who played a free-to-play action RPG in the last decade. It features action combat, a roster of diverse heroes that you assemble to form teams, and a large pretty world to explore where you’ll also get to meet new characters.

Speaking of which, while Origin has its own original story, expect to be teaming up with characters from the series - some of whom wouldn't be able to meet naturally. You can thank the game's multiversal story for that.

Beyond all the serious business of saving the world and battling monsters, The Seven Deadly Sins: Origin also has a cozy, relaxing side. You’ll be able to fish, cook, forage and take on the beauty of the world with your pals.

The game has a bit of an unusual release schedule. It’s set to arrive on PC, PS5, iOS, and Android. PC (Steam), and PS5 players will be able to jump in starting March 16, whereas the global mobile launch is scheduled for one week later, on March 23.

You can pre-register right now on the official website if you’re interested in earning a few rewards when the game introduces. You can, of course, always wishlist the game on Steam and the PlayStation Store, too.

Look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a fresh Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month! This class is called the Sisters Novitiate, a group of wonderfully violent women with a penchant for crossbows, burning people alive and putting a stop to anyone that dares to oppose the God-Emperor. Neato!

According to a blog post accompanying the reveal of the class, the Sisters Novitiate work a tad differently compared to other classes available in the game. "Unlike other classes, the Sisters Novitiate are able to choose from six divine and devastating Acts of Faith, as opposed to blitz and combat abilities," the post explains. "Their abilities draw upon reserves of Faith, allowing them to unleash brutal Neural Whip attacks to the inspiring Icon of Purity and protective prayers. Faith can take many forms for the Sisters Novitiate, each channeling the Emperor's divine will and bringing his wrath upon his enemies.".

Industry observers note that you build up their Faith while fighting, in turn choosing from a selection of doctrines and pledges in their talent tree, "each shaping how Faith is both accumulated and put to use. Any two Acts of Faith can be equipped at a time, allowing players to choose how their Novitiate will unleash righteous fury on the battlefield." I mentioned crossbows, right? Well, I stand lore corrected, as what they technically have is the Condemnor Stakethrower, which "pins what remains of their enemies to the walls." They do also have access to a flamethrower, a significant ole mace, your classic sword and shield, and whatever the hell a "Penitent Eviscerator.".

In a recent development, this DLC class also comes the same day as a free upgrade, which will introduce the Metlagun, equipable by the Sisters Novitiate as well as the Veteran. Apparently there'll be more information on the free update soon. Oh, and the release date! It's December 7th, so a little under a month away. I'm sure you can (Dark)tide over the next few weeks by rewatching the gnarly reveal trailer.

10 Glitches and Bugs Plaguing GTA 6 at Launch

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1379 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dualshockers

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, every upcoming game has its… quirks.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 is still fresh, and people are jumping into it as I write these words.
  • Planes fly through buildings, cars teleport onto the highway, and it doesn’t seem to be bound to one console, as Xbox and PlayStation consumers have both been reporting these issues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, every upcoming game has its… quirks. This is especially true in the modern era of gaming, as many games now release with game breaking glitches and bugs that have an effect on how people enjoy it.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is still fresh, and people are jumping into it as I write these words. While on the surface the game looks like magic, many people have been finding numerous bugs that have destroyed their experience.

Planes fly through buildings, cars teleport onto the highway, and it doesn’t seem to be bound to one console, as Xbox and PlayStation consumers have both been reporting these issues.

Textures and environments can be tricky, especially when you have a map that is as massive as the one in GTA 6. There are bound to be some barriers that end up becoming a bit glitchy, and players have found plenty of them.

There have been a number of reports that players have been glitching into walls inside buildings, and it seems to mostly happen when fighting.

Recent findings suggest that not all walls are affected, as it seems to only affect interior, lower cut walls, and not full size interior walls or exterior boundaries. Still it is pretty awkward when you want to fight someone and you both end up teleporting into a wall.

In a recent development, okay, so not taking damage isn’t necessarily a bad thing, but in the world of GTA, where things are supposed to be realistic, it is kind of strange. It would be nice to not take damage at times, but it enhances the realism of the experience.

Sources indicate that cars have always been a bit of a tricky thing, and they are still a bit tricky in GTA 6. Players have reported being able to teleport out of their car while flying down a street without taking damage.

Recent findings suggest that normally, you are supposed to dive from the car, but instead, players have said the character model just teleports out of the vehicle and starts running on the road until they come to a stop. It’s a bit strange.

Sources indicate that some players have noticed a peculiar thing while flying planes in GTA 6, and that is that they sometimes don’t respect the laws of physics, allowing them to phase through objects. It doesn’t happen a lot, but it is weird when it does happen.

It could be intentional, because it seems to only happen to large buildings, but it wasn’t like that in GTA 5, so it probably wasn’t an intentional choice.

Players have noticed that when they jump out of a plane, it seems to phase through all the buildings around it, allowing it to just crash into the ground instead of hitting the building and falling like it used to.

Cops can now tase you in GTA 6, and it is pretty amusing to watch yourself get tased. Just like in real life, it locks up your character’s muscles, and it makes them fall to the ground helpless. Shortly after, they are free to stand back up.

In a recent development, unfortunately, not every player has been able to stand back up, as some have noted that they get stuck in the ground after getting tased. Their character model clips into the pavement, causing them to get stuck in place for a while before their character gets released.

This can be a bit jarring, but it isn’t something that completely breaks the game. It just makes things a little easier for the police to catch you.

According to recent reports, early in the game, Donnie is taken hostage. The game uses this as an opportunity to teach you about stealth and combat. It’s a nice little tutorial that is very engaging. Unfortunately, some players have reported that they need to restart this level because the game breaks for them.

It has been revealed that when sneaking around the enemies, you will spot a cage. This cage has a tendency to be a bit buggy, and sometimes you will get pulled into it if you decide to take cover against it.

This traps you inside the cage, unable to get out, and therefore, unable to complete the mission. The only thing that is worse is that if the enemies know you are in there, you basically become an easy target.

People have been waiting 13 years to get their hands on GTA 6. It has been one of the most talked about games of the last decade, and some people can’t even get into the game. Others who can, have it crash on them shortly after launch.

According to recent reports, this isn’t a console specific glitch, though I have seen more people say they have a PS5 when it comes to the crashing issue. The issue is that the game automatically crashes shortly after launch.

According to recent reports, people have mentioned that they have tried to rebuild the database, and have even redownloaded the game, and nothing has worked. It is okay for some bugs to occur, but the game crashing every time you try to play it is entirely different.

Getting wanted by the police is a common occurrence in any GTA game, but things are a bit different in GTA 6. The cops are more lively, and they notice more things. There are a lot of systems in place to make the entire experience more thrilling.

Industry observers note that well, these same systems tend to bug out a bit right now, and they bug out by giving you an infinite wanted level. Well, almost infinite, as there is a way to remove the wanted level.

In a recent development, there have been reports of players being stuck with a wanted level for hours despite clearing all of the complications with it. The only way to get it to end seems to be to go to sleep. Getting stuck being wanted in an area for hours sounds like a huge inconvenience.

Sources indicate that this is a bug that is affecting both consoles, but seems to be affecting Xbox more than PlayStation. Players have reported objects spawning as they drive at high speeds. By this, I mean cars will magically appear, so will NPCs, and other items.

GTA 6 is a massive game, and it could be that the loading has not been completely optimized, and when driving at very high speeds, the game may not be able to keep up with the load times.

I am not a tech wizard, so I don’t know exactly what causes it, but I do know that it has been bothering a lot of players, and they want it fixed ASAP.

This is an glitch that appears to mostly be affecting those who are playing GTA 6 on the Xbox Series S, but there have been reports of players being unable to load textures and models, resulting in these low-poly models that are reminiscent of graphics you’d see on PS1 era games.

Everything turns blocky, the faces lose all texture, and all that can be made out is the basic shape of the body, some scraps for clothes, and the hair.

It’s a shame that this is happening to people, and it reminds many of the crazy problems that were happening when Cyberpunk 2077 first rolled out. Odds are, it can be fixed with an revision, but for the time being, it sets a bad example.

A major part of any GTA game is committing crimes, and one of the many crimes that you will commit frequently is murder. This is mostly against gang members and other criminals, but it still counts, and you need these people to be able to take damage.

Sources indicate that you also sometimes need to stop an NPC by hurting them and not killing them. Unfortunately, there is a bug that makes NPCs bulletproof, and some players have been saying they are emptying entire clips into an NPC for not a single bullet to affect them.

This breaks the game because it makes it so you can’t complete some missions. It is an urgent issue that Rockstar should fix so people can beat the game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Sources indicate that of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

In a recent development, things are officially looking better for Marathon. The game’s Server Slam, essentially an open beta that’s freely available everywhere, has kicked off. This is the last chance for anyone curious about Bungie’s next significant game to play it before it officially goes on sale next week.

Considering how unpopular the game has been throughout its development, and judging by the feedback from earlier closed beta tests, the turnout for the Server Slam is definitely encouraging.

In a recent development, the Marathon Server Slam has been online for a little over 12 hours on Steam, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. Only one of those platforms shares player numbers, of course, but it's enough to offer some visibility into how popular the test has been.

In a recent development, immediately after servers went live, Marathon shot up the Steam most played charts. The game quickly achieved a peak of 143,621 concurrent players (via SteamDB), which is very respectable. Given that the Server Slam will be available for the entire weekend, there’s every chance the numbers will go up.

Sources indicate that these figures are particularly encouraging when you look at Arc Raiders, the current top dog in the extraction shooter space, and the game that stole Marathon’s thunder last year when the two of them were being promoted by their publishers. Marathon, of course, got delayed out of 2025, which allowed Arc Raiders to launch first. It, of course, ended up proving that extraction shooters can be mainstream hits.

Like Marathon, Arc Raiders hosted its own server slam just a few days before its launch. That open test attracted 189,668 concurrent players at its peak, which is not that far off from Marathon’s so far.

Assuming positive word of mouth continues, more players are bound to jump in over the weekend and perhaps get Marathon to match or even exceed Arc Raiders’ record. At any rate, this is good news for beleaguered Bungie and points to what could be a substantial launch.

Marathon arrives March 5 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S.

Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.

In a recent development, as his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:.

Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

Cleanser Man won out among the six finalists, a few of which were also cleaning-themed bosses. “In the end, we chose Cleanser Man because of the unique way the concept was brought together and the originality of the color design,” claims game director Shinya Ikuta. “While staying true to and respecting the original submission, we adjusted certain details to better fit the world and style of the game.”  Unfortunately, Capcom has not revealed Cleanser Man's creator, but you can see the character in action in the reveal video below.

According to recent reports, in addition to Cleanser Man, Mega Man: Dual Override's rogues' gallery includes the following revealed robot masters: Twinkle Girl, Jet Man, Tank Man, and Cook Man. The remaining three bosses have yet to be revealed.

Sources indicate that mega Man: Dual Override launches in 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, PlayStation 4, Xbox One, Switch, and PC. Recent findings suggest that is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

Industry observers note that the latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's important because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

In a recent development, beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history.".

According to recent reports, perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era.
  • In a recent development, the two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17.
  • The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Sims 4 has officially entered into its paid mods era. Developer Maxis announced The Sims Maker Program, and The Sims 4 Marketplace - two new destinations to publish, and discover new add-on content.

In a recent development, the two new features will arrive first on PC and Mac, starting March 17. PlayStation and Xbox players will receive them over the next couple of months, which is very much in line with how other franchises have rolled out their own paid mods systems.

The Maker Program is a way for community creators to get their work out there, and profit from it. The content they create will end up on the Marketplace, where other players can browse it, and pay for it if they want to use it in their game.

It has been revealed that created content will be available across all platforms. All previous packs The Sims 4 players should be familiar with will move to the Marketplace, too: once the feature launches, this is where you’re going to find Expansion Packs, Game Packs, Stuff Packs, Kits, and other official additions created by Maxis.

Sources indicate that alongside this, the game is also introducing a upcoming virtual currency - Moola - which is what you’re going to use to purchase Maker Packs, as well as Sims 4 Kits in the Marketplace. A portion of your purchase will go to the creator (roughly 30%) of what you buy.

Industry observers note that it is worth noting, however, that you’ll still be able to buy Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs without having to purchase Moola, or go through the Marketplace. Kits are the only items that will no longer be available on the existing PC/console storefronts. Moola comes in the usual denominations you’ve seen a hundred items in other games’ in-game shops.

Industry observers note that in order to start creating custom content and publishing it on the Marketplace, you’ll need to first be accepted into the program. Once that’s done, you’ll be able to directly publish your content on the Marketplace.

It has been revealed that in the blog post announcing the fresh features, Maxis stated that creators will have control over the price of their content, and how it's packaged. These are referred to as Maker Packs, which can include Create-a-Sim or Build/Buy items.

Industry observers note that you can apply to become a Maker from March 5. Once accepted, you’ll also get access to the Maker Suite, which is what you’re going to use to test your work to ensure it runs smoothly on the different platforms, and eventually publish it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer.
  • "After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts.
  • It has been revealed that on Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

"After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years.".

It has been revealed that on Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox announced earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

It has been revealed that if you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he announced the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

Recent findings suggest that "Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material.".

"You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," says ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...].".

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • One of the coolest easter eggs found in GTA 6 so far is the Kraken, the legendary sea monster from Norse and Scandinavian Folklore.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you want to see this easter egg for yourself, this guide has everything you need to know.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Grand Theft Auto series is well-known for its easter eggs, and GTA 6 is no different. Some notable ones include Dexter’s apartment from the hit TV show, UFO sightings, and even nods to Red Dead Redemption 2.

One of the coolest easter eggs found in GTA 6 so far is the Kraken, the legendary sea monster from Norse and Scandinavian Folklore. While the Kraken sighting in GTA 6 isn’t exactly a living creature, but rather just a structure near the ocean floor, it is clearly a reference to the famous sea monster.

Recent findings suggest that if you want to see this easter egg for yourself, this guide has everything you need to know. Here’s how to find the Kraken in Grand Theft Auto 6.

Sources indicate that the Kraken can be found underwater, south of Catalan Bay and east of Peacock Bay in Vice City. The exact location of the Kraken can be found in the image below.

The water map can be a bit tricky to read due to there being no land, structures, or streets, but if you look closely enough, you will notice that there are distinct shapes within the water.

Sources indicate that the Kraken is located on the second oval-like shape down from the beach of Catalan Bay. The oval shapes represent large sand hills and rocks underneath the water’s surface.

When you reach the location shown in the image above, equip your scuba gear and dive downward until you reach the sand. Next, take a look around you until you spot a strange-looking structure. You may have to swim a bit in case your diving point wasn’t the exact correct location.

Upon approaching the structure, you will immediately notice that it looks like a ship tangled in the Kraken’s tentacles. Unfortunately, the tentacles don’t move or anything, but it’s still a really cool easter egg that just goes to show how much love Rockstar Games put into GTA 6.

In case you need some help actually diving deep enough to reach the Kraken in GTA 6, we've got you covered on how to find scuba gear.

Recent findings suggest that there are a few ways to acquire scuba gear. First, you can find scuba gear on the small dock behind Jason’s house in Chapter 1, which is the earliest method. However, this method becomes unavailable to you if you have completed the first chapter.

In a recent development, another way to get scuba gear is by exploring docks near beaches. While not all docks will have scuba gear to grab, a good number of them do.

It has been revealed that you can also get scuba gear from boats that are either docked or sailing the seas. I recommend visiting Kenton’s Charter Boat in Key Lento since it always has spare scuba gear on its seats.

Keep in mind that once you are finished scuba diving for the Kraken, or just scuba diving in general, and return to dry land, the scuba gear will eventually despawn. In other words, you will have to find more scuba gear the next time you want to go scuba diving.

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

According to recent reports, mycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite promptly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

Industry observers note that for starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Recent findings suggest that different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create fresh effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:.

Recent findings suggest that as is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint.

The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the organization's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be revealed tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.

It has been revealed that last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.

Sources indicate that what do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

  • In a recent development, the rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

Recent findings suggest that as spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

In a recent development, the rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a upcoming lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

It has been revealed that torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

Nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Cyber Monday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026.

If this will be your first Black Friday shopping at Amazon, there are some basic things you need to know about Amazon sales:.

You can share your Prime membership with family members using Amazon Family.

You can set price alerts for products you want, and your Alexa devices can notify you when they go on sale.

But if you only take one bit of advice for shopping on Amazon, let it be this one: Don't buy anything you weren't going to buy anyway. A good way to make sure you do this is by making a list of the products you do want, and only having eyes for those.

Black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

In a recent development, nowadays, both large retailers and small businesses compete for Black Friday shoppers, so you can expect practically every store to run sales through Monday, Nov. 30, 2026. The “best” sales depend on your needs, but in general, the biggest discounts tend to come from larger retailers who can afford lower prices: Think places like Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, and Home Depot. You can find all the best sales from major retailers on our Black Friday coverage.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that you're less likely to see throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech.

'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (698 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time.
  • Sources indicate that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox.
  • Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Sources indicate that now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

No matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar says that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.".

Industry observers note that PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

Recent findings suggest that while PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

In the post, Rockstar also announced that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

Industry observers note that that's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar indicates that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

Again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the manufacturer hasn't explained why that is.

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the firm's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the firm, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

In a recent development, alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

Industry observers note that "While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

In a recent development, "Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982.".

Sources indicate that that certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent organization Microsoft are still right now subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

"Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. InXile is the studio behind the Wasteland series, and is currently working on Clockwork Revolution.

Tech Report: 10 Best Games That Showcase The Xbox Brand

💡 Key Takeaways

  • These days, however, in the wake of poor direction during the Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S eras, Xbox is struggling to retain a healthy gamer population, with many gamers choosing instead to play games on Nintendo or PlayStation due those platforms’ vast variety of exclusive titles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Microsoft’s gaming brand, Xbox, has finally reached the momentous milestone of existing for 25 years, with all four generations of Xbox console greeting gaming memories that will last lifetimes for those who played them throughout the 21st century.

These days, however, in the wake of poor direction during the Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S eras, Xbox is struggling to retain a healthy gamer population, with many gamers choosing instead to play games on Nintendo or PlayStation due those platforms’ vast variety of exclusive titles.

With Xbox having recently reached its 25th anniversary and the next generation of Xbox consoles, Project Helix, expected to debut in a few years, here’s a look back at 10 exclusive games that best showcase the Xbox brand and may potentially entice people to try an Xbox console.

Many fans of the British game developer, Rare, likely recognize them for creating Nintendo-centric titles like Banjo-Kazooie or Donkey Kong Country but under Microsoft’s ownership, one of the best games they ever released was Viva Piñata.

A life simulation game, Viva Piñata is set on the wondrous Piñata Island and has players restore a garden there with the goal of attracting, raising, and defending the local population of living piñata animals so that they can be eventually shipped off across the globe to become the center of attention at parties.

Viva Piñata encapsulates how creative, fun, and unique Xbox games can be and, while there hasn’t been a latest Viva Piñata game in over 18 years, people today can still easily play it and other classic Rare games via the compilation Rare Replay.

One of the best games that showcases the absolute power and capabilities of modern Xbox consoles is Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, the latest entry in the long-running Microsoft Flight Simulator series.

Like many flight simulator games, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 allows players to learn how to fly planes in both first and third-person but this game is the most advanced flight simulator yet as players can learn how to fly other real and fictional aircraft in numerous locations across the globe.

For example, people can fly Halo’s Pelican dropship over Yosemite National Park, the Goodyear Blimp over London, a DG Flugzeugbau DG-1000 over Mount Fuji, a Airbus Helicopters H225 over the Stilt Villages of Papua Upcoming Guinea and more.

Viva Piñata was very memorable but it wasn’t the most popular video game Rare made under Microsoft’s ownership, with that title instead going to the hit cartoonish pirate multiplayer game Sea of Thieves.

Played primarily in first-person, Sea of Thieves allows players to create and customize their very own pirate and ship as they set sail alone or with a crew of friends into monster-infested waters in search of treasure and glory across the sea.

Sea of Thieves might have had rough start when it first rolled out in 2018 but in the years since, it has truly shined to become the definitive pirate multiplayer experience thanks to its comedic gameplay and eventful updates adding upcoming areas to explore and supernatural sea creatures to fight.

For a while, Xbox was the best platform to play western RPGs on and, during the original Xbox era, one of the best exclusive games to showcase this status was Bioware’s legendary Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic.

A third-person round-based RPG, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic is set roughly 4,000 years before the events of the Star Wars films and follows an amnesiac warrior as they set out to stop the Jedi turned Sith Darth Malak from conquering the galaxy with the mysterious Star Forge.

While KOTOR’s gameplay hasn’t aged perfectly in the 23 years since its launch, its story, characters, and world designs have remained immaculate, with its characters going on to influence many other Star Wars stories and it still featuring one of the greatest gaming twists surrounding the character of Darth Revan.

Since the days of the Xbox 360, Microsoft has often invested and supported small game developers with immense potential, leading to the release of games like Braid, Ori and the Blind Forest, and the subject for this entry, Cuphead.

Studio MDHR’s debut title, Cuphead is a 2D run and gun game with visuals inspired by rubberhose-style cartoons of the 1920s and 30s, similar to Steamboat Willie, following the brothers Cuphead and Mugman as they set out to collect soul contracts from various bosses in order to save their souls from the Devil.

While Cuphead was only a timed exclusive on the Xbox One, it represents the brand’s ability to support small game development studios and uplift experimental titles into gaming stardom as Cuphead has gone on to sell millions of copies and become a highly successful multimedia franchise.

Racing has always been at the core of Xbox gaming from the early days of Project Gotham Racing to the more modern Forza Motorsport titles and while none of these games have been as popular as Mario Kart, one has managed to become the most advanced, realistic racing game yet: Forza Horizon 6.

The latest entry in the ongoing Forza Horizon series, Forza Horizon 6 has players take to the urban and rural streets of Tokyo, Japan in over 500 cars as they strive to qualify for the Horizon Festival or simply explore the many beautiful landscapes of Japan alone or with friends.

In a similar way to how Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 became the premier modern flight simulator, Forza Horizon 6 has become the premier realistic racing game thanks to its hyperrealistic visuals, vast automotive and track customization options, and dynamic environments.

KOTOR is one of the best RPGs to ever debut on an Xbox console but it’s not the brand’s premier exclusive RPG, with that honor instead going to 2004’s Fable and the greater Fable franchise.

Originally pitched to be a fantasy RPG that would have allowed players to have kids in-game, and witness plant life grow among other promises, the original Fable wound up being a very charming, British humor fantasy RPG following a young boy as he set out to become the hero of Albion.

While the first Fable didn’t meet all of its creator, Peter Molyneux, aspirations, it sequels did slowly start to achieve all of Molyneux’s promises and more, becoming the source of many fond memories to the point that Forza Horizon 6’s own Playground Games is rebooting the series with 2027’s Fable.

One of the most recent games that best showcase the Xbox brand’s storytelling capability and multiplayer potential is The Coalition’s Gears of War: E-Day, the sixth mainline entry in the Gears of War series and prequel to the first Gears game.

Like its predecessors, Gears of War: E-Day is a third-person cover shooter with updated maneuverability but what made it really shine is its emotional story following COG soldiers Marcus Fenix, Dominic Santiago, Mags Carter, and Lucas Reyes as they face the first horrifying Locust invasion on Emergence Day.

Gears has always been known for its gory, action-packed gameplay as well as its heartfelt story following people face seemingly insurmountable nightmarish forces and E-Day proves that Gears can still deliver horrifying, emotional yet hopeful gaming narratives 20 years after its first debuted in 2006.

The Xbox 360 era was arguably Xbox at its best and most successful largely in part due to Microsoft investing in several permanent and timed exclusive titles alike, such when Microsoft and Mojang worked together to make the Xbox 360 the first console home for the global sensation that was Minecraft.

While Minecraft was already highly popular on PC, Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition helped introduce millions of console players to the blocky survival game for the first time via Xbox Live Arcade in 2012 and led many to grow up with the game as it evolved and expanded with every upgrade.

Minecraft: Xbox 360 Edition’s success ultimately led to Microsoft acquiring Mojang in 2014 and since then, the two companies have worked together to make Minecraft one of the most successful multimedia franchises of all time through the release of numerous Minecraft updates, spinoffs, and adaptations.

The Halo franchise is as integral to Xbox as Sonic the Hedgehog is to Sega and Super Mario is to Nintendo and while there have been many fantastic Halo titles released over the years, I would argue that the best entry in the series to showcase the Xbox brand is the FPS prequel, Halo: Reach.

Bungie’s last Halo title, Halo: Reach has players embody the customizable Spartan-III Noble Six as they join the Spartan-II and III squad of Noble Team in defending the human military world of Reach from an alien Covenant invasion a few months before the events of Halo: Combat Evolved.

While Reach’s campaign is a ton of fun on its own, I believe Reach is the best Halo title to represent the Xbox brand because it remains the most complete Halo title to date as it released with four-player campaign co-op, playable Elites, Firefight, Forge, Theater, Infection, Grifball, and more fun modes and features.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.
  • Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the massive Diablo 4 Developer Patch has indeed delivered the goods. One of the livestream’s big topics was, of course, the game’s upcoming mini-season, which is set to kick off next week and run until the launch of Lord of Hatred, the game’s anticipated next expansion.

You can tell Blizzard wanted to have a bit of fun with Season of Slaughter, as many of its major features make it look like a limited-time event, but there is plenty to be excited about here.

Season of Slaughter kicks off March 11, and will run until the following season kicks off April 28, with the launch of the Lord of Hatred expansion. Many of the season’s biggest additions were available to preview in the 2.6.0 Public Test Realm.

In a recent development, patch 2.6.0, as you might have guessed, is the one that will kick off the slaughter next week. The headline feature here is ability to become The Butcher, the iconic in-game boss who randomly invades players’ games.

It has been revealed that when you play as The Butcher, you’ll be rewarded the more kills you get in quick succession. Your skills hotbar will transform to become something more fitting of The Butcher, making them more brutal. You’ll also earn a seasonal currency as you play.

Starting the seasonal questline is how you can begin to assume The Butcher’s form. A Taste of Power can be initiated from Gea Kul. Transforming into The Butcher can be done in a few ways. As you play, you’ll earn Meaty Offerings, which can later be spent on Shrines of Slaughter in the fresh Helltide. Once activated, the shrine will draw more enemies towards you.

Industry observers note that if you never venture into PvP zones in Diablo 4, this season may change your mind. The standard PvP combat that could only be found in Fields of Hatred has been replaced with a Ceremony of Slaughter, a upcoming event that rewards you for killing enemies rapidly. See it through and The Butcher’s Idol will spawn, allowing you to transform into it.

Elsewhere in the world, you’ll also be able to attain the same power at Slaughterhouses, a latest activity type available this season. Inside, you immediately become The Butcher for the entirety of the run.

The Butcher’s arrival also ties into two of the other Season of Slaughter’s more interesting additions. First, the Killstreak system finally arrives in Diablo 4, rewarding you for being as efficient as possible in carving your way through enemies.

Industry observers note that anyone who played Diablo 3 should be familiar with how it works. It kicks off the moment you get a kill, and has a visible timer where you’ll need continue performing the same action to up your streak. The more kills you get, the more often your timer will refresh.

It has been revealed that there are five tiers to climb through: Killstreak, Carnage, Devastation, Bloodbath, and Massacre. You’re awarded for the tier you manage to reach before the timer runs out. You’ll earn XP and seasonal rep each time a Killstreak is achieved.

The other Butcher-themed addition is Bloodied Items, which is a new item quality available throughout this season. They play into the Killstreak system to grant you even more power. Bloodied Items come with unique affixes that scale off your Killstreak tier. You’ll see many familiar items in that pool, as any item in the game has a chance to drop as Bloodied. Bloodied Items can also be acquired by earning Fresh Meat.

In a recent development, even if none of that sounds exciting, you’re probably going to redownload the game for The Paladin free trial, which kicks off alongside the upcoming season on March 11. The trial is only available until March 18, and it lets you try out the Paladin class.

The trial is available across PC, PlayStation, and Xbox. You’ll be able to take the upcoming class for a spin, but your progress will be capped at level 25. The Paladin can be permanently unlocked by buying the Lord of Hatred expansion, as it’s one of two classes the expansion is introducing.

The good news is that any progress you make in the free trial will carry over to the full game if/when you buy the expansion.

Season of Slaughter also kicks off a Doom: The Dark Ages collaboration event. As we’ve come to expect, there’s a very limited free component to the collaboration, in the form of the Doom Reliquary. This is essentially a mini-battle pass that includes the Shield Saw skin, Slayer’s Flair, the head of the Cyberdemon as a back trophy and various other smaller bits.

Sources indicate that the more impressive items - such as character skins, will instead be available to purchase for real money. The list includes the Doom Slayer armor, Mecha Dragon Serrat skin for your cat mount, and a Cacodemon pet.

Though the armor skin is cross-class compatible, judging by how much previous collaboration items have cost in Diablo 4, most of us probably won’t be spending that kind of money to get it.

  • The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Upgrade to actually see it in action.

According to recent reports, the Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

Sources indicate that the Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

Industry observers note that the Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

Recent findings suggest that the Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside newly introduced Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the major day.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that but then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski.
  • Industry observers note that in development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our fresh galactic overlords!".

Industry observers note that but then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

Industry observers note that in development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Recent findings suggest that outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

According to recent reports, you can read more on Steam. Release date there is currently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

EA hires another former Call of Duty boss to take the lead on all Battlefield Studios' projects
